question: At the plenary session on 8 February 2024, a number of MEPs reiterated their demand for transparency concerning the links between the Commission and the tobacco industry. The Commission focused on the doubts surrounding the choice of Dentsu as the service provider for the European traceability system, reinforcing our concerns about opaque practices and potentially problematic relationships.

This debate was in fact only the latest in a series of repeated vain attempts to finally obtain clear answers from the Commission on this important matter. The Commission’s speech stressed the importance of respecting the rules when renewing the contract with Dentsu in June 2023. However, no information was provided on the initial selection process for the service provider. 1.
How does the Commission explain the choice of Dentsu as service provider in 2018 and the extension of its contract in 2023?
Where can we find the results of the evaluation that led to the choice of the service provider and its extension?
Who were the other candidates examined by the Commission to be in charge of the European traceability system?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.7.2024) 1. The appointment of Dentsu as the secondary repository’s operator in the tobacco traceability system does not fall within the scope of the public procurement rules inter alia because the services are neither offered to the Commission nor are paid by the EU budget.

In accordance with transparent and non-discriminatory rules and procedures described in the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/5741, the secondary repository’s operator is appointed from among the providers of primary repositories.

Being one of the providers of primary repositories at the time of the opening of the procedure by the Commission, Dentsu was eligible to submit an offer for appointment as the secondary repository operator. Dentsu was selected on the basis of objective criteria determined in the selection procedure. 2.

In line with Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/574, the result of the appointment of the secondary repository’s operator was made publicly available by the Commission on its website2. The procedure for the selection of this operator is described in Part B of Annex I to the Implementing Regulation. 3.

Information concerning the names of the tenderers in any offer submitted, including for the appointment of the secondary repository operator, is treated confidentially. Only the companies that were providers of a primary repository at the time of the opening of the procedure by the Commission could participate in the procedure for the appointment of the secondary repository operator.
The current list of the primary repositories’ providers can be found on the Commission’s website3.
